The lake

Fixed. The previous version drew the reflection above the waterline and clipped it away, and had its depth mask on backwards. Both are documented traps, both are explained at the bottom. Scroll down. Ripple removes the displacement filter so you can see what it contributes; box-reflect swaps the whole hand-built version for the one-line WebKit property, which does nothing in Firefox.

Program Analysis

Symbolic Execution

02 June 2026 · Nine minutes

Symbolic execution is a means of analyzing a program to determine what inputs cause each part of it to execute. Instead of running the code on real values, an interpreter walks it while holding every input as a symbol.

It arrives at expressions written in terms of those symbols, and at constraints for the outcome of each conditional branch. Where concrete execution answers what a program does with 5, symbolic execution answers what it would take to reach a place at all.

A worked example

int f() {
  y = read();
  z = y * 2;
  if (z == 12) fail();
  else printf("OK");
}

During symbolic execution the program reads a symbol, λ, and the branch condition becomes the constraint λ * 2 == 12. Execution forks, and a solver later returns 6 to reach fail().

Limitations

Merge states that differ only in irrelevant ways and you accept weaker constraints. Bound the loops and you accept incompleteness past the bound. Prioritize paths heuristically and the interesting one may be starved.

Engines worth reading next: KLEE and angr.

The two bugs, and why they are worth knowing

A negative scaleY maps the box away from its origin. With transform-origin: top, a point at y lands at -0.62y — above the top edge, outside the water, clipped by overflow: hidden. Nothing errors; the lake is simply empty. The fix is to position the copy inside the water and flip it with the default centre origin, so it mirrors within its own box.

A transform applies to the element's mask as well as its pixels. After scaleY(-1) the source-bottom is what appears at the top, so a mask written black → transparent fades the reflection at the waterline and leaves it solid in the deep — backwards. Written in source order it has to be transparent → black. This one is easy to stare past, because it looks deliberate. 

.lake {
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
  height: clamp(130px, 20vh, 190px);   /* crop = foreshortening */
}

.reflection {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
  transform: scaleY(-1);               /* default centre origin */
  filter: url(#ripple);
  mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom,
                transparent 6%,        /* inverted: this is the DEEP end */
                rgba(0,0,0,.5) 46%,
                rgba(0,0,0,1) 100%);   /* and this is the waterline */
}

The words for it, in English

waterline
The horizontal line where the solid page stops and the water begins. In the sense used here it is the boundary itself, not the water.
foreshortening
An object appearing shorter along the axis pointing away from the viewer. A reflection lying flat on water is foreshortened; that is why you see less of it than of the thing reflected.
falloff
How quickly something fades with distance — light, a shadow, a reflection. "A soft falloff" fades gradually, "a hard falloff" ends abruptly.
anisotropic
Having different properties in different directions. The ripple noise is anisotropic because its frequency across is not its frequency down, which is what stretches it into bands.
iso-lines
The contours joining points of equal value in a field. A plain gradient has straight or circular iso-lines; warping it makes them irregular.
sheen
A soft, low, spread-out reflectivity on a surface — not a highlight, which is small and bright. Water has sheen; polished metal has highlights.
to read as
Design shorthand for "to be perceived as", regardless of how it was made: "the noise reads as dirt", "gold on every link reads as wallpaper". The single most useful phrase in this vocabulary.
to carry
For an element to do the work of communicating something: "space and light carry the theme", "the left rule carries the code block". Its opposite is decoration, which carries nothing.
to spend
To use up a limited budget of attention: "gold is spent once, on the title". Implies you now have less of it left, which is exactly the idea.
to date
To become recognisably of its period, and so to look old: "heavy ornament dates fastest". Not the same as looking bad — it looks like 2026 rather than timeless.

Per page, not per site

You are right that the design can differ by page, and the lake is the argument for it: on every post it would be a tic, but on one page it is a place. The honest candidates, in order — the 404, where the reader has reached the end of the world and a shore is the right metaphor; About, which is the one page whose job is atmosphere rather than information; and the home gate, seen once per visit. Behind a post it would flatten the atmosphere, the same objection design.md §15 already records against full-bleed header images.

Two costs that do not go away. It is a second ambient animation if you switch Drift on, and design.md §11 permits exactly one — the flame. Leave it static. And the flame plus its reflection is two golds, so with one link under the cursor the page is at the three-per-viewport ceiling with nothing spare.
